content_html_sanitized:
Analysis by Richard Cowan

This morning on Steve Kubby’s show on Blogtalkradio.com, our guest was Marc Emery,

who is still fighting extradition to the US.

See

Program Notes for the MarijuanaNews “Global Conspiracy Report” August 3, 2005 US

Fails To Get Marc Held Without Bail. Mexico The Real Problem. Kubby Zings Czar.

Interview with Michelle Rainey.

It was a wide-ranging conversation that focused on his support for Ron Paul and other

libertarian matters, but we also talked for a bit about the market for “BC Bud.”

Readers may recall –

but let me remind you anyway – that I have been almost alone in

questioning all of the talk about how much stronger it is and how big the market for it

might be. I even called it “BS Bud.”

See

Behind the BS: Ian Mulgrew’s Bud Inc. – A Look Inside BC’s Big Biz.

and

Time Magazine Reports BC Bud 20% Less Potent Than Four Years Ago?? Incompetent

Prohibitionist Propaganda and Even Worse Journalism. As Some Reporters Die to Find

the Truth Others Live to Lie.

and links

One reason that I was flying solo on this subject was that it was in almost everyone’s

interest to exaggerate its importance.

For the prohibitionists, it was just one more scare story to get more power and money. For

the current Administration it also helped divert attention away from the huge problems

created by a very real “drug war” in Mexico,

See

Will “Plan Mexico” And Its Surge in the Drug War Put Prohibition On the Public

Agenda? Analysis by Richard Cowan

and perhaps from meth as well.

See

Meth and Marijuana. Now: How the Narks Created Crank in Canada. The Iron Law of

Drug Prohibition. The Inescapable Economics Of Contraband.

In 2003, Walters was devoting a huge amount of time to the subject.

See

“John Walters’ Testimony To The Canadian Parliament.” The Public Record Or What

He Would Have Said, If He Was Not Afraid of Being Asked Embarrassing Questions.

The Battle for Canada.

As the above linked article illustrates, the US was also very concerned that Canada might“decriminalize.” He needed have worried about the invertebrates in Ottawa, and several of

the States on the Canadian border passed decrim laws back in the ‘70s.

The same prohibitionist propaganda campaign was going on inside Canada. The Canadian

narks are as addicted to lying and lustful for power as their American counterparts, but at

least the Americans were not subordinating our sovereignty like the Canadian

collaborators.

See

Voice of America Becomes Latest Organization to Be Corrupted By Cannabis

Prohibition. Canadian Collaborators Lie To Undermine Their Country’s Freedom and

Sovereignty. The Myth of BC Bud.

and

Would BC Have Less Bud if It Had More Prisoners? Lying to Canadians To Support the

Cannabis Prohibition.

In any case, as a result of the prohibitionist propaganda, as well as post-9-11 laws, there

was a significant tightening at the border, which increased the risks of getting caught, but

the business went on – at whatever level – because there was still money to be made.

From 2000, for pre-9-11 risks,

see

INS Report On Canadian Border Uses Numbers to Deceive, But Ends by Contradicting

Party Line.

and

A Leading Marijuana Lawyer Explains How the System Really Works – A Must-Read,

Especially for Canadians.

During all of this nonsense, BC growers also had an incentive to exaggerate. It was just

good marketing, with the Czar helping them. After all, what could be better than having

the US government warning the public that your product is too “good”?

And then, there is the Czar’s steno pool, AKA the media.

See

How The New York Times Misleads Americans About the Canadian Marijuana

Situation.

and

Front Page Fantasy: The New York Times Pushes Fact Free Journalism Supposedly

About “BC Bud”

and the link above about Time magazine.

But what US and Canadian narks could not stop, a collapsing Greenback did. When I first

went to Canada in 1999, the Canadian dollar was at its lowest point at about 62 US cents.

Vancouver was wonderfully cheap, and so was BC Bud. Today, the Loonie, as the

Canadians call there dollar (because of their bird, not their politicians), is just below par

with the US.

Consequently, the profit margins have all but disappeared while the risks have increased.

Now, if there was a surplus of BC Bud as a result of the drop in exports, the price of

cannabis in Canada should drop in C$ terms, but that has not happened. The price ispretty much the same.

Marc suggested that Canadians may have increased their cannabis consumption, already

the highest of any major country.

“Canada was Number One (Numero Un, since Quebec

did more than its share) in cannabis consumption in advanced countries. According to the

UN, 16.8 per cent of Canadians aged 15 to 64 used marijuana last year.”

See

International “Prohibition Situation Report” – DEAland Media Ignore News Showing

Cannabis Prohibition Is Counterproductive. Coffee Shop System Survives.

Marc said that he thinks that exports to the US could not have been more than 20% of the

Canadian production, which is far less than the 50% to 90% that was suggested by the

prohibitionists and their parrots in the media.

Do the math…

If Canada really does produce cannabis worth $5 billion or more, and most of it is

consumed domestically, and it has one tenth the population of the US, which has

comparable levels of per capita consumption, then the US market would be roughly ten

times that amount. Estimates for cannabis production in Mendocino County alone run as

high as $7 billion. (California’s population is about 10% greater than Canada’s.)

Of course, Mexican commercial, which is getting better, supposedly makes up about half of

the US supply, but it sells for much lower prices than domestic, so that might bring the US

total dollar value down to $30 billion or so.

I think that that number is very low, but it is still three times the “official estimates.”

However, the point is that no one really knows anything for sure except the seizure

numbers along the Mexican border. We don’t really have a good idea how much is seized

every year in the US in conjunction with the 800,000+ arrests.

In short, we only know that the cannabis market is in the tens of billions of dollars and that

it has increased consistently even after (or because of) decades of state violence and an

unprecedented propaganda campaign.

Is the only lesson here that we have been lied to?

No, it is that lies have purposes and consequences. I am happy to brag about having been

right about BS Bud, but I very much regret having been right about the reason for the lies.

Canadians are now faced with living in a prohibitionist police state.

See

Wake Up Canada! 2006 Canadian Professional Police Association Political Agenda.

“Prime Minister of Canada to Open the CPPA Annual Legislative Conference”

More on that soon.
